name: His Bundle Tachycardia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for His Bundle Tachycardia

criteria.description: Narrow QRS tachycardia with a rate typically between 120-180 bpm and absence of AV dissociation
Demonstration of tachycardia originating from the His bundle region during invasive electrophysiological study
Termination or transient slowing of tachycardia with adenosine administration
No evidence of underlying structural heart disease on imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic ECG findings plus confirmation by electrophysiological study
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on invasive electrophysiological testing due to similarity with other narrow complex tachycardias.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; cardiac biomarkers typically normal unless secondary ischemia occurs
imaging: Normal echocardiogram excluding structural heart disease; Holter monitoring showing narrow complex tachycardia episodes
genetic: No well-established genetic mutations identified; idiopathic in most cases
other: Electrophysiological study demonstrating tachycardia originating from the His bundle region

distinguishingFeatures: Typical AVNRT shows AV dissociation and different response to adenosine
Electrophysiological study localizes reentry circuit to AV node rather than His bundle
Usually associated with structural heart disease

redFlags: Signs of heart failure or cardiomyopathy
Sudden onset of chest pain or ischemic symptoms
references: Zipes DP, Jalife J. Cardiac Electrophysiology: From Cell to Bedside. 7th Edition. 2018.
Wellens HJ, et al. Electrophysiologic characteristics of His bundle tachycardia. Circulation. 1981.
